title: Adaptive incident propagator with contextual enrichment for PD/Slack
creator: Elena Garcia
description: Build an adaptive incident propagation service that takes enriched observability events (traces, metrics, logs), deduplicates and classifies them, and creates scoped PagerDuty incidents and Slack notifications with contextual runbook attachments. The service should support automatic postmortem draft creation when incidents resolve, include trace/span evidence links, and be configurable per-customer and per-route to control noise and PII exposure.
acceptance_criteria: An incident event pipeline consumes normalized observability events (OpenTelemetry+metrics aggregation) and produces PagerDuty incidents with a consistent title template and severity mapping
Slack alerts are delivered to the configured channel with an actionable summary card and links to traces, logs, and the console incident page
Deduplication reduces duplicate incidents by at least 60% on test workloads (simulated burst scenario)
Runbook attachments (canonical runbook + route-specific checklist) are attached to PD incidents for P1/P0 only
Post-incident automation creates a draft postmortem in the company Confluence template prefilled with incident timeline, top spans, top error messages, and links to PRs/related issues
Config flags exist to avoid sending any PII to third-party services and toggle enrichment levels per customer tier
technical_notes: Ingest pathway: observability events -> Kafka topic 'incidents-ingest' -> enrichment worker group -> incident-router service
Tracing hooks: annotate root spans with 'incident.candidate' tag at the runtime layer (serving runtime) and emit a lightweight incident event to avoid heavy rehydration of full spans
Enrichment sources: trace context, KV cache lookup for model/route metadata, recent feature-flag state, and quota/customer tier from Customer Service (cached)
Classification model: initial rule-based mapping with thresholds (error rate, latency p95, payload size) with later plan to add a lightweight ML classifier (future work)
PagerDuty mapping: severity = {P0: outage, P1: degraded, P2: warning} configurable via project settings; include dedupe key = route+model+window
Slack notifications use message blocks with buttons: Acknowledge (opens PD), Open console incident, Attach runbook, Create quick issue
Security: secrets for PD/Slack stored in KMS; outbound webhooks are VPC-restricted for Private deployments; enrichment must scrub PII per data-classifier rules
comments: 2026-03-05 - Elena Garcia: Created ticket to centralize incident propagation logic; goal is reduce alert noise and improve mean-time-to-resolution by improving context in PD incidents.

2026-03-07 - Ravi Menon: Spike found that naive per-span enrichment triples processing cost; moving to metadata-first approach (trace id + top span ids) to limit payloads. See spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/INC-Propagation-Spike
2026-03-09 - Marco Liu: Design review feedback - suggested using Kafka compacted topic for routing config and having the router read policy changes without restart. Added to technical notes and plan.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (SRE): Ran simulated burst (1000 errors/min) against staging ingest; dedupe rules reduced PD volume by ~62% when window=120s. Raw results and dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/incidents/ingest-burst

2026-03-11 - Security review (initial): flagged potential PII in span.attributes.request_body. Decided to add a data-classifier pass to drop request bodies and only include hashed identifiers for correlation. Ticket for scrub rules: ENG-18305
2026-03-12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/incident-propagator/pull/189 - initial worker + router. Code owners: @rmenon, @mliu. Needs unit+integration tests against a PD mock.
2026-03-14 - Elena Garcia: PM sign-off on MVP scope; postpone ML classifier to follow-up cycle. MVP will ship rule-based classification with config UI and PD/Slack integrations.
Follow-ups: add per-customer silencing windows, enable enrichment sampling for high-volume customers, and add telemetry for incident suppression effectiveness
success_metrics: Reduce PagerDuty incident count from observability sources by 40% (measured week-over-week) for noisy non-actionable alerts
Improve median time-to-ack by 20% for P0/P1 incidents due to enriched context
Postmortem draft creation on 95% of incidents classified as P0/P1 in staging
release_notes: MVP: Add incident propagation service that routes enriched observability events to PagerDuty and Slack, attaches canonical runbooks, and drafts postmortems on resolve. Admins can configure severity mappings and enrichment levels in the console.
